_note: Read by scripts/report.py plan, which picks a few items per session by seed. Items are angles and scenario seeds, never lines to speak: the panel writes fresh wording every time.

moves.drill: go one step deeper per question until a floor or Staff
moves.twist: change one constraint (ten times the load, another region, a new compliance rule) and ask what changes
moves.compare: set two options side by side and ask when each wins
moves.teach-back: ask them to explain it to a new joiner, then probe the part they glossed over
moves.counter: take the opposite position and ask them to defend theirs
moves.quick-fire: two or three short questions on the thread, no follow-ups

Leslie: the exact mechanism behind the claim
what happens when two requests or writers hit it at once
which guarantee the underlying system actually gives
how they know it is correct beyond the tests passing
why this data model and not a neighbouring one
what a partial failure or retry does to the result
how the contract stays compatible for existing callers
where ordering or time assumptions could break
Dennis: how they found out it was broken
what a rollback would have looked like
what it costs to run, and who pays
the smallest guard that would have caught the failure
what was invisible in the dashboards at the time
where the capacity limit is and what hits it first
how far a failure spreads and what contains it
what the on-call person does at the first alert
Freda: what was traded away to get there
who disagreed and how it was settled
which scope they would drop under a tighter deadline
how the impact was measured after launch
how the decision was made and by whom
what they would change about how the team worked
how they explained it to a non-engineer
who owned it after launch and what that cost

snippet_bugs: resource not closed on the error path
integer overflow in a running sum
exception swallowed in a catch block
mutable internal state returned from a getter
list modified while iterating over it
diagnosis_scenarios: latency climbs with no deploy and no traffic change
memory grows slowly over days until a restart
intermittent 5xx errors start after a deploy
a queue consumer falls further behind every hour
CPU spikes at the same time every day
the database connection pool is exhausted under normal load
one region is slow while the others are fine
requests time out only for the largest customers
a disk fills up on one node
errors start right after a certificate or clock change
walkthrough_shapes: one user request, from the client to storage and back
one record, from ingestion to the report that shows it
one code change, from commit to running in production
one alert, from the page to the post-mortem
one schema change, from pull request to live traffic
one new customer, from sign-up to first real use
background_openers: the decision in their career they would make differently today
the path from their first engineering job to the current one, in turning points
the project they are proudest of and why it mattered to the business
what changed in how they work between their first and their latest role
the kind of problem they keep getting pulled into, and why
what a colleague would say they are the person to ask about
